correctness.rationale: For 0<a<1 and fixed a<r<1, the normalized monomial norm (1+a^{n+1-m})/(n+1) gives the kernel series. The inside scale a^{1-m}K tends to (1-s/a)^(-2), zero-free on |s|<a. On the fixed annulus a<|s|<1, K/(m s^m) tends locally uniformly to the bilateral 1-psi-1 sum Phi_a. The Ramanujan product has neither zeros nor poles there and one negative winding due to (1+1/s); since K/(m s^m) has winding -1, the argument principle gives exactly m-1 zeros in |s|<r for large m with no boundary zeros. Local subharmonic convergence of m^-1 log|K| to max(log a,log|s|) and the Laplacian give equidistribution of those m-1 zeros on |s|=a. Spot-check: two sampled windings (11 and 19 for m=12,20) and bilateral-product discrepancy 4.1e-12; not an infinite certificate. No assertion about boundary layer or uniform m thresholds.
